title: A celebration of Three Rivers Stadium, perfectly named and perfectly flawed - The Athletic
content: # A celebration of Three Rivers Stadium, perfectly named and perfectly flawed. Three Rivers Stadium had the perfect name. For all of its history — it was home to four Super Bowl champions, two World Series winners and even a Stanley Cup celebration — there were at least twice as many reasons Pittsburghers couldn’t wait to see it replaced. And that Pittsburgh thing where fans leave games early no matter the score, that started at Three Rivers Stadium. Its predecessor might not have been the equivalent of a mausoleum, because no mausoleum had sections that swayed like the ones wheeled into place for Steelers Sundays, but Three Rivers Stadium was a place where something truly unbelievable had to happen for it to become a lasting memory. It was one thing for each of the cities’ new stadiums to look like one another, but if either of the stadiums should have had “river” in its name, Pittsburgh’s should have been the one.

The complex would be built entirely above water.**  Proposed New Sports Stadium - 1958  **A proposal submitted in 1958 for a Pittsburgh stadium built entirely above the Monongahela River.**  **Eventually, the north shore was chosen as the spot for the new "Pittsburgh Stadium." The complex would include hotels, restaurants and a riverfront park to complement the new state-of-the-art multi-purpose stadium.**  **The original prototype was a bit different from the final design. The cost of the stadium was $55 million.**  **In between the ground-breaking and the completion of construction, the structure was given a new name, "Three Rivers Stadium." The Pirates left** **Forbes Field** **after sixty-one years and moved into their new home in July 1970.
